title: HOSA Nutrition: Vitamins and Minerals - Nutrition - Application
subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient is taking **Warfarin** (Coumadin), a blood thinner. Which vitamin intake should be kept consistent to avoid interfering with the medication's efficacy?
questions.explain: Warfarin works by inhibiting Vitamin K-dependent clotting factors. Sudden changes in dietary Vitamin K (e.g., leafy greens) can alter the drug's effect.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: To maximize the absorption of **non-heme iron** (from plant sources), a dietitian should recommend consuming it alongside foods rich in:
questions.explain: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) enhances non-heme iron absorption by reducing iron from the ferric ($Fe^{3+}$) to the ferrous ($Fe^{2+}$) state, which is more soluble.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with **chronic alcoholism** is admitted with confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia (Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome). Which vitamin should be administered immediately?
questions.explain: Alcohol inhibits thiamine absorption and utilization. Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome is an acute thiamine deficiency requiring immediate IV thiamine.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A client asks about sources of Vitamin A. Which of the following foods contains the highest amount of preformed Vitamin A (retinol)?
questions.explain: Preformed Vitamin A (retinol) is found in animal products like liver. Plant sources like carrots contain provitamin A carotenoids, which must be converted by the body.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which cooking method typically results in the **greatest loss** of water-soluble vitamins (Vitamin C and B-complex)?
questions.explain: Boiling causes water-soluble vitamins to leach out of vegetables into the water, which is often discarded. Steaming or microwaving preserves more nutrients.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient with **osteomalacia** (soft bones) should be advised to increase intake of fortified milk, fatty fish, and:
questions.explain: Osteomalacia is the adult form of Rickets, caused by Vitamin D deficiency. Sunlight allows the body to synthesize its own Vitamin D.
questions.subject: Nutrition
